title: Implement & Analyze a Sorting Algorithm
description: Generate a working implementation of a sorting algorithm with step-by-step explanation and complete Big-O complexity analysis.
template:
You are a Computer Science tutor specializing in algorithm design and analysis. I need you to help me understand and implement a sorting algorithm.

Algorithm: {algorithm_name}
Programming language: {language}
Constraints: Assume the array can be any size and contain duplicates.

Please provide:
1. A clear explanation of how {algorithm_name} works (2-3 sentences)
2. A complete, working implementation in {language} with inline comments explaining key steps
3. A complexity analysis table with:
   - Best-case time complexity and scenario
   - Average-case time complexity
   - Worst-case time complexity and scenario
   - Space complexity and explanation
4. One short example trace showing how the algorithm processes [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]

Format the complexity analysis as a structured table. Ensure the code handles edge cases like empty arrays and single-element arrays.

title: Trace & Debug a Search Algorithm
description: Execute a search algorithm step-by-step, showing state changes and identifying bottlenecks or bugs.
template:
You are a code debugger specializing in algorithm execution tracing. I need you to trace through a search algorithm's execution.

Algorithm: {algorithm_name}
Input array: {array_input}
Target value: {target_value}

Please provide:
1. A step-by-step execution trace showing:
   - The current state of pointers/indices at each step
   - Which elements are being compared
   - Any decisions made (e.g., which branch is taken)
2. A trace table with columns: [Step #, Action, Current Index/Pointer, Comparison, Decision]
3. The final result (element found/not found, number of comparisons)
4. A brief analysis: Is this the most efficient search for this data? Why or why not?

Make the trace clear and detailed enough that I can follow exactly what the algorithm does. Highlight any inefficiencies or unnecessary comparisons.

title: Convert Problem to DP Recurrence & Solution
description: Break down a problem into overlapping subproblems, derive the recurrence relation, and implement an optimized DP solution.

title: Analyze Big-O Complexity of Code
description: Analyze arbitrary code to determine time and space complexity, identifying dominant operations and worst-case scenarios.
template:
You are an algorithm complexity analyst. I need you to analyze the Big-O time and space complexity of this code.

Programming language: {language}
Code:
```
{code_snippet}
```

Please provide:
1. Time complexity analysis:
   - Break down the code by section (e.g., each loop, each recursive call)
   - For each loop/recursion, identify how many times it executes (as a function of input size n)
   - Identify the dominant term and give the overall Big-O time complexity
2. Space complexity analysis:
   - Account for all variable storage, arrays, recursion call stack, or data structures used
   - Give the overall Big-O space complexity
3. Detailed explanation of why certain operations dominate (e.g., "the nested loops dominate because...")
4. Best-case, average-case, and worst-case scenarios with brief explanation of when each occurs
5. If applicable, suggest if there's a faster algorithm for this problem

Format the analysis clearly with code annotations if helpful. Explain your reasoning step-by-step so I can verify each claim.

title: Translate Pseudocode to Code with Edge Cases
description: Convert algorithm pseudocode into working code with explicit edge case handling and verification.
template:
You are a code implementation specialist. I need you to convert pseudocode into working code.

Algorithm pseudocode:
{pseudocode}

Programming language: {language}
Input constraints: {constraints}

Please provide:
1. A direct translation of the pseudocode into {language}, keeping the same logical flow
2. Inline comments explaining what each section does
3. Explicit edge case handling for:
   - Empty or null inputs
   - Single-element inputs
   - Boundary conditions (e.g., off-by-one errors)
   - Any constraint violations mentioned above
4. A test suite with at least 5 test cases:
   - 2-3 normal cases
   - 1-2 edge cases
   - Expected output for each
5. A brief explanation of any optimizations or modifications you made from the pseudocode

Ensure the code is production-ready and handles all edge cases gracefully without crashes or undefined behavior.
